scope: fix-restore-schema-drift backend (tools/restore.mjs: Flyway version check, backend restart after restore, storage note)

findings.title: Message for a schema that is still behind after the restart can name the wrong cause
findings.resolution: fail() after the restart reads the version separately: undefined says the version could not be read and points to the logs; only a read version that is behind gets the image-older text.

findings.title: Logs hint on restart failure leaves out the compose project
findings.resolution: Logs and restart hints share composeHint (-f <compose.yaml> [-p <project>]). BackupRestoreIT asserts "-p <project> logs backend".

findings.title: Migration IT builds a full backend image inside the IT run, so the test is heavy and slow
findings.reason: Deliberate: the defect is Flyway-at-startup behaviour of the real backend, so the IT builds the real image from this checkout in a throwaway project (Docker layer cache keeps it to ~1 min); a fake backend would not prove that V4 is re-applied. BackupRestoreIT runs in the Failsafe phase like the other Docker ITs.

findings.title: The target version comes from the checkout, not the running image, so a checkout older than the image leaves a mismatched schema and exits 0
findings.resolution: The expected version is the newer of the checkout migrations and the schema version read before the restore, so a running image newer than the checkout is restarted too (design decision 6).

findings.title: Task 3.5 'Archive; commit' is ticked, but the change is not archived
findings.resolution: Tasks not yet done were unticked in 13e1f9b; 3.x are ticked only as each completes (archive is task 3.5 in the archive commit).

findings.title: Task 3.3 is ticked, but review-findings.json does not exist
findings.resolution: Unticked in 13e1f9b; this file is now persisted and dispositioned before task 3.3 is ticked.

findings.title: Task 3.1 'qa:verify green' points at verification evidence this change did not regenerate
findings.resolution: Unticked in 13e1f9b; qa:verify is re-run after the fixes and its regenerated report is committed with the archive.

findings.title: The 'schema still behind after restart' failure path omits the manual restart step and the 'data is restored' message
findings.resolution: Every post-commit failure goes through fail(): "the data is restored, but …" plus the next step; the still-behind path prints a project-aware rebuild (compose up -d --build --wait backend with --project, npm run stack:up otherwise).

findings.title: The post-commit failure branches (exit 1 + manual step) have no test
findings.resolution: New IT "when the restarted backend cannot migrate the restored schema, restore exits 1 and says the data is restored" (crash-looping backend: exit 1, data-restored text, restart and logs steps).

findings.title: Undocumented drift: the tool exits 1 on an unreadable version or an unknown backend state even when no restart may be needed
findings.resolution: The MODIFIED requirement now states the exit-non-zero outcome whenever the check cannot complete (version or backend state unreadable, restart/healthcheck failed, schema still behind).

findings.title: The MODIFIED requirement exists only in this repo's change delta; its presence in the docs-store spec could not be verified
findings.reason: Not applicable: the docs store has no platform-foundation spec (`openspec show platform-foundation --store doucko` → not found); platform-foundation is this repo's own spec (its Purpose: "this spec covers this repository's part"). NFR-10 itself is unchanged and no contract operation changes.

findings.title: Unguarded JSON.parse in the health wait can crash with a stack trace after the restore has committed
findings.resolution: backendContainer() catches JSON.parse errors and returns null; the wait keeps polling until its deadline.

findings.title: Reading the checkout's migrations is not guarded and can throw after the commit
findings.resolution: latestMigration() runs before the safety backup and the restore; a failure there exits 1 with "nothing was changed".

findings.title: A dump with tables but no flyway_schema_history counts as 'behind' and restarts a working backend into a crash loop
findings.resolution: A restored schema with tables but no flyway_schema_history now warns and restarts nothing (design decision 7); an empty schema is still restarted.

findings.title: An uncaught JSON.parse in the health wait prints a stack trace after the restore has committed and loses the 'data is restored' message
findings.resolution: Same fix as F12: no stack trace after the commit; a failed wait ends in fail() with the data-restored message.

findings.title: The tests for scenario 'Restored schema and checkout disagree without a restart' do not check that nothing was restarted
findings.resolution: Scenario narrowed to "no backend running"; both tests assert the output lacks "restarted now".

findings.title: The printed manual restart command leaves out the compose file that the tool itself uses
findings.resolution: The printed commands include -f "<compose.yaml>" and -p <project>, matching composeArgs().

dispositionNote: The run stopped at --max-total-usd 10 ($10.75): 3 verify steps were skipped, and 4 findings were rejected by verifiers. Every persisted finding is dispositioned.
